questions.question_text:
Four valid cuts on a network have capacities $54, 48, 62, 51$. These cuts include a minimum cut.
What is the maximum flow of the network?

options.why: Selected the first cut capacity instead of the minimum cut capacity.
Selected the maximum cut capacity instead of the minimum cut capacity.
Selected the second-smallest cut capacity instead of the minimum cut capacity.

questions.question_text:
A network has a maximum flow of $65\text{ L/min}$.
A proposed cut $C$ has capacity $78\text{ L/min}$.
Is cut $C$ a minimum cut?

options.text: No, because its capacity ($78$) is greater than the maximum flow ($65$).
Yes, because $78$ is the largest capacity in the network.
options.why: Mistakenly believed the minimum cut corresponds to the largest capacity value.

options.text: Yes, because any valid cut equals the maximum flow.
options.why: Confused the minimum cut with general valid cuts of larger capacity.

options.text: Yes, because $C$ is the only cut named, so it must be the minimum one.
options.why: Treated the single cut given in the question as automatically minimal, instead of testing its capacity against the maximum flow of $65$.

questions.solution_text: By the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem, the minimum cut capacity must equal $65$. Since $78 > 65$, it is not minimal.

questions.question_text: According to the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem, what does the capacity of the minimum cut represent?

options.text: The maximum possible flow from source to sink.
The average flow along all source-to-sink paths.
options.why: Confused the bottleneck capacity with an average of path flows.

options.text: The sum of all edge capacities in the network.
options.why: Confused the minimum cut capacity with the total network weight.

options.text: The minimum capacity of a single individual edge.
options.why: Confused the minimum cut with the smallest individual edge weight.

questions.solution_text: The capacity of the minimum cut equals the maximum possible flow through the network.

questions.question_text:
A directed network has edges $SA = 40$, $SB = 45$, $AC = 30$, $BC = 20$, $BD = 24$, $CT = 42$ and $DT = 38$, directed in the order of their letters.
Four valid candidate cuts, including a minimum cut, are: Cut 1 ($\{SA, SB\}$, capacity $85$), Cut 2 ($\{AC, BC, BD\}$, capacity $74$), Cut 3 ($\{CT, DT\}$, capacity $80$), and Cut 4 ($\{CT, BD\}$, capacity $66$).
Which set of edges forms the minimum cut?

options.text: $\{CT, BD\}$ with capacity $66$
$\{SA, SB\}$ with capacity $85$
options.why: Selected the source cut instead of identifying the minimum capacity cut ($66$).

options.text: $\{CT, DT\}$ with capacity $80$
options.why: Selected the sink cut instead of identifying the minimum capacity cut ($66$).

options.text: $\{SA, CT\}$ with total capacity $82$
options.why: Added $40 + 42 = 82$ for edges that do not form a complete cut: the path $SBDT$ remains; the minimum cut is $\{CT, BD\}$ with capacity $66$.

questions.solution_text: Cut 4 separates $\{S,A,B,C\}$ from $\{D,T\}$ and has capacity $42 + 24 = 66$. The listed cuts include a minimum cut, and $\min(85, 74, 80, 66) = 66$, so edges $\{CT, BD\}$ form the minimum cut. The maximum flow is $66$.

questions.question_text:
A valid cut crosses two edges directed from the source side to the sink side with capacities $24$ and $31$, and one edge directed from the sink side to the source side with capacity $10$.
What is the capacity of the cut?

options.why: Included the reverse edge, calculating $24 + 31 + 10 = 65$.
Subtracted the reverse capacity instead of excluding it, calculating $24 + 31 - 10 = 45$.
Selected the larger forward edge capacity instead of adding both forward capacities.

questions.solution_text:
Count only edges directed from the source side to the sink side.
$\text{Cut capacity} = 24 + 31 = 55$.
The reverse edge of capacity $10$ is excluded.

questions.question_text:
In a network, the edges leaving source $S$ have a total capacity of $90$, the edges entering sink $T$ have a total capacity of $82$, and an internal cut has a capacity of $76$. The internal cut is a minimum cut.
What is the maximum flow?

options.why: Assumed the sink inflow is always the minimum cut without checking internal cuts.
Assumed the source outflow is always the maximum flow.
Added source and sink capacities ($90 + 82$) instead of finding the minimum cut.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the edges crossing the minimum cut from source to sink when maximum flow is achieved?

options.text: They are fully saturated with flow.
They always have unused excess capacity.
options.why: Mistakenly assumed bottleneck edges have spare capacity.

options.text: They carry zero flow because they are cut.
options.why: Confused an imaginary mathematical cut with physical destruction of edges.

options.text: They only carry flow if all edges have equal capacities.
options.why: Invented an unwarranted condition of equal edge capacities.

questions.solution_text: At maximum flow, all edges crossing the minimum cut from source to sink are fully saturated.

questions.question_text:
In a gas pipeline network, a minimum cut crosses three pipes directed from the source side to the sink side with capacities $180$, $150$ and $120\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$, and one pipe directed from the sink side to the source side with capacity $60\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$.
What is the maximum flow rate of the network?

options.text: $450\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$
$510\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$
options.why: Included the reverse pipe capacity, calculating $180 + 150 + 120 + 60 = 510$.

options.text: $390\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$
options.why: Subtracted the reverse pipe capacity instead of excluding it, calculating $180 + 150 + 120 - 60 = 390$.

options.text: $120\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$
options.why: Selected the smallest forward pipe capacity instead of summing the forward capacities across the minimum cut.

questions.solution_text:
Exclude the reverse pipe.
$\text{Minimum cut capacity} = 180 + 150 + 120 = 450\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$.
By the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem, the maximum flow rate is $450\text{ m}^3/\text{h}$.

questions.question_text:
A network has four candidate cuts: $C_1 = 120, C_2 = 105, C_3 = 112, C_4 = 130$. These cuts include a minimum cut.
What is the maximum flow?

options.why: Selected the first cut rather than the minimum cut.
Selected the second-smallest cut rather than the absolute minimum.
Selected the maximum cut capacity instead of the minimum cut capacity.
